Hi John / Alice —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Scope we discussed: Private/VPC deployment for inference serving, customer-managed VPC peering, no public egress for inference traffic, and retention controls for PII in telemetry/logs.
- Action items for Redwood:
  1) Provide a network/data-flow diagram for the private deployment (we'll attach a draft).
  2) Clarify what telemetry/logging Redwood keeps by default (tokens, metadata), retention defaults, and options to disable or redact PII.
  3) Confirm egress controls and how to enforce deny-by-default egress from the inference nodes; provide approaches for on-prem/air-gapped installs.
  4) Provide sample contract language for data residency and SOC2 evidence pointers.

I've attached an initial VPC/data-flow diagram and our private deployment checklist — please review and call out any missing pieces.

Proposed next meeting: Dec 20 at 9am PT to walk the diagram and agree on redaction/retention defaults. If that works for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifying Qs before the 20th: 

1) PII redaction: can Redwood provide an option to strip or hash any user identifiers before writing to logs/usage metrics? We need a mechanism that prevents persistent PII in any observability store.
2) Retention: default telemetry retention in hosted mode is fine, but for private deployments we need to set a 90-day retention maximum for logs with PII unless a longer retention is explicitly approved. Is that configurable per-deployment?
3) Egress controls: we need assurance that inference nodes will not attempt DNS lookups or HTTP requests to the public internet except to customer-managed endpoints (e.g., private artifact registry). How do you enforce that and what OS-level tooling do you use for on-prem installers?

I can have our infra lead (Alice) join the 20th call to go deeper on the VPC diagram. Procurement is CC'd for timing on the PO.

John
John Doe
Head of Information Security, AcmeHealth

Subject: Fwd: AcmeHealth - Private VPC egress & data residency follow-up

Marissa / team —

Looping in Dev to address the on-prem/air-gapped install requirements and Neha to outline our telemetry retention/redaction options. Preliminary notes below based on the ask: 

-- Dev: For air-gapped / on-prem installers we provide an offline bundle with all runtime artifacts and a small agent that performs local health checks. Network policy enforcement is primarily left to the customer's firewall / host-level iptables; for additional protection we can ship an egress-blocking iptables profile and a DNS policy stub. Also possible to run inference inside a sealed Kubernetes namespace with egress policies enforced at the CNI level (Calico/NetworkPolicy).

-- Neha: By default our private deployments enable structured request/response logs (request_id, model, latency, token_counts) but we do not persist full request text unless explicitly enabled. We offer PII redaction hooks: a pre-logging filter that can hash or remove configured fields, and a configurable retention window per deployment (default 30 days, can be set to 90 days for enterprise accounts). We can also provide a short runbook for customers to rotate/clear logs on schedule.

I'll prepare a short appendix addressing the three numbered items from John and attach before the 20th meeting.

-Nikhil

John / Alice —

Quick update ahead of our call in 30 mins: attached a short appendix with the specifics Nikhil flagged (redaction options, retention defaults) and an expanded notes section on egress controls for on-prem. High-level answers to your three questions: 

1) PII redaction: yes — pre-logging filter available. Options: drop full request text, hash identifiers, or field-mask configured keys. We can ship the redaction filter as part of the deployment and provide a sample Helm value to toggle.
2) Retention: configurable per-deployment — default 30 days, can be set to 90 days (we will include this as a deployment variable and in the contract exhibit).
3) Egress controls: enforced by default via network policy + optional host iptables profile for on-prem. For air-gapped installs we do not enable any external telemetry by default; all artifact pulls are via customer-provided registry or offline bundle.

Next steps:
- Confirm whether Acme prefers 30 or 90 day default for telemetry on initial rollout (please reply to the thread).
- We'll update the VPC diagram with the names of your internal endpoints and post the revised diagram to the Drive link.
- Legal/procurement: I'll have our contracts manager prepare exhibit language for data residency and retention for review this week.

If that covers everything, I'll capture these as the official answers and attach the appendix to the shared folder.

Best,
Marissa
